# Opaque Native Restart and Saved-Input Replay

## Scope and Authority

Tools #5470 supplies typed transport for native state that cannot be represented
truthfully as a named numeric state vector. The wire format is
`native-state-replay/1.1.0`. Its complete initial-state authority is a native
artifact descriptor and separately resolved immutable payload bytes. Numeric
observations are deliberately absent from this restart authority. The existing
`experiment-replay/1.0.0` numeric reader and semantics remain unchanged; that
reader rejects the native envelope instead of discarding hidden state.

These are interchange contracts, not a physics solver or qualification system.
UpstreamDrift #11921 owns actual R2025b decoding, independent integration,
model coverage and acceptance. All required engine/model rows remain visible.

## State, Model and Runtime Identity

`NativeStateArtifact` binds format/version and expected decoded native class,
exact producing runtime/provider, source and loaded-model SHA-256 values,
native clock, solver and effective configuration/checksum policy, byte size,
payload digest and explicit complete-native-restart or observables-only role.
`NativeReplayModel` preserves inventory model/variant identity and ordered input
mapping separately. Native artifacts cannot substitute an observables-only
scope during replay admission.

`freeze_native_state_artifact` verifies an owned immutable byte snapshot. It
rejects wrong size/hash and numeric/list coercion; it never deserializes or
executes the payload. A consumer must load these verified bytes and independently
verify actual decoded class, time, runtime and model compatibility. Hashing MAT
bytes identifies one serialization; it does not establish canonical semantic
state encoding, source-to-binary equivalence or transitive library closure.

## Native Clock and Input Boundary

The saved native `snapshot_time_seconds` and `start_time_seconds` are finite and
ordered, with an explicit native clock identity. Saved input histories reuse
the existing interval-relative time and interpolation contracts. Native replay
time is the saved snapshot plus each relative input time; the operating point
is never retimed to zero. Overflow or loss of strict ordering at native floating
point precision is rejected. Requested intervals and an explicitly supplied
solver step must also survive translation to the native epoch within the larger
of 1e-9 relative interval error or 64 ULPs of that interval. Epoch ULPs never
relax this policy. Consumers must check effective native solver precision too. Physical input units, muscle excitation versus
activation, force versus command, and explicit contact identity remain governed
by the shared `InputHistory` and `ReplayExecutionPolicy` contracts.

## Integrity and Failure Semantics

`NativeReplayIntegrity` retains shared component hashes and adds an entire
envelope digest, including experiment identity. Strict JSON rejects duplicate
or unknown fields, unsupported versions and stale integrity. Capability
availability remains distinct from declared support; required unavailable or
unsupported capabilities remain blockers. Metadata equality does not prove a
native engine followed the declared policy.

## Native Consumer Requirements

For R2025b, preserve hidden Simscape/block state, solver/execution state and
operating-point compatibility. Disable block reduction before capture and bind
effective solver settings rather than unresolved UI values such as `auto`.
Verify a nonzero-time saved/reloaded restart against uninterrupted native
integration, including discrete/hidden state. Preserve wrong model/runtime/time,
tampered or missing blob, stale artifact and observable-downgrade negatives.
No state reset is permitted during the requested saved-input replay horizon.

## Evidence and Remaining Work

Initial missing-module, coercion, public-facade, duplicate-key and experiment
identity failures were observed before fixes. The current focused suite passes
77 tests, including 23 unchanged numeric T01 tests and 11 native JSON Schema tests. Astra review supplied
reproduced string-channel coercion and large-epoch interval-retiming negatives;
both failed before correction. Configured source typing passes. The schema reuses stable numeric-contract
definitions by local reference. The manual renderer uses the pinned toolchain;
QA inspects every actual page and rejects missing, duplicate or reordered page
records as the manual grows. Inventory/governance/normal hooks and actual
R2025b integration remain pending at this development checkpoint. This chapter
does not approve a scientific calculation or manual release.

## Primary References

[MathWorks R2025b ModelOperatingPoint](https://www.mathworks.com/help/releases/R2025b/simulink/slref/simulink.op.modeloperatingpoint.html)
defines native restart state and the read-only snapshot clock; its numeric
logged-state view excludes internal Simscape state.
[MathWorks R2025b Operating-Point Workflow](https://www.mathworks.com/help/releases/R2025b/simulink/ug/model-operating-point-for-faster-simulation.html)
documents compatibility and effective configuration constraints. These native
claims require separate actual execution evidence from UpstreamDrift.
